title: Re-run: 200 items detect a 5-point gap in ~22% of comparisons
summary: An independent re-implementation (new script and seed) of one cell of the paired-bootstrap power simulation: 200 binary items, ~70% base accuracy, a true 5-point gap and shared-difficulty mixing rho 0.5 — the 95% CI excludes zero in 22.5% of 1000 comparisons (SE 1.3 pp), median half-width 7.75 points.

statement.text: At 200 binary-scored items, about 70% base accuracy and a true 5-point gap, with item-level correlation between the arms about 0.25, a percentile paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero in about 22% of comparisons (median half-width 7.75 points).
qualifiers: One cell of the original grid; 1000 trials x 1000 percentile-bootstrap resamples, seed 16102026.
doesNotClaim: Anything about other sample sizes, baselines or correlations.
That a real benchmark has this item correlation.

unknowns: Behaviour with clustered or duplicated items

testedScope.summary: stdlib Python simulation, seed 16102026, 1000 trials x 1000 percentile-bootstrap resamples, n=200, gap 5 points, mixing rho 0.5.
